name: Question 18
worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨2,-2,1⟩,\,p=⟨5,0,3⟩,$ and $q=⟨1,1,-1⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨5,0,3⟩-⟨2,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨3,2,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨1,1,-1⟩-⟨2,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,3,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-10i+4j+11k \\  & =⟨-10,4,11⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ & =⟨5,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ & =-17\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ & =-17 \\ -10x+4y+11z & =-17 \\ 10x-4y-11z & =17 \\ 10x-4y-11z-17 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the position vectors of the points A,P and Q are a=⟨2,−2,1⟩,p=⟨5,0,3⟩, and q=⟨1,1,−1⟩.

First, using the 3 points we build 2 vectors parallel to the plane:

v1=AP→=⟨5,0,3⟩−⟨2,−2,1⟩=⟨3,2,2⟩v2=AQ→=⟨1,1,−1⟩−⟨2,−2,1⟩=⟨−1,3,−2⟩

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of v1 and v2 as follows:

n=v1×v2=[322]×[−13−2]=ijk322−13−2=−10i+4j+11k=⟨−10,4,11⟩

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−10,4,11⟩=⟨5,0,3⟩⋅⟨−10,4,11⟩r⋅⟨−10,4,11⟩=−17

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨−10,4,11⟩=−17−10x+4y+11z=−1710x−4y−11z=1710x−4y−11z−17=0.
